deep.reconstruction:
Context: cote 154 studies 'systèmes de pseudo-droites', i.e. pseudoline arrangements X in the projective plane. X̃ appears to be a 2-dimensional cell complex whose cells are the possible positions of an additional pseudoline D relative to X. This is essentially the space of one-element extensions of the arrangement.

This page fixes a dictionary between the cells of X̃ and the type of position of D:
- 2-cells (faces) of X̃ are 'stable' positions, meaning D is in general position with respect to X.
- Oriented faces are oriented stable positions.
- 1-cells (edges) are 'semi-stable' positions, presumably D passing through exactly one vertex of X.
- 0-cells (vertices) are 'critical' positions, presumably D passing through two or more vertices of X.
- Oriented vertices are oriented critical positions.

Next he defines 'arêtes biorientées', called repères. A repère is a quadruple (D, s, ω, σ̄):
- D is a critical position;
- s is a point of S_D = D ∩ S, i.e. a vertex of X lying on D;
- ω is an orientation of D;
- σ̄ is an orientation (local side or sense) of X at s.
The page then restates this as 'D with a repère of position: (D, S_D), +'.

A map from repères to oriented faces is started: (D, s, ω) ↦ 'la position voisine stable obtenue en ...', unfinished. That is, one pushes D off the vertex s in the direction given by the orientation data; the top-right sketch shows a pseudoline crossing a triangle's apex and moving upward (arrow, labelled σ), a triangle-flip / mutation picture.

The first line recalls from p.134 that on X̃^ex there are four operations σ1, σ, σ2, σ0 on these flag-like objects, with consecutive ones commuting. This is a cyclic analogue of the cartographic-group presentation of a map (flags with involutions σ0, σ1, σ2, where σ0 and σ2 commute).

Purpose: to give X̃ a combinatorial-map / flag description, so that its topology can be computed via a 'cartographic' group action on repères. The next page shows him computing explicit chains of positions D_1, ..., D_20 around vertices s_i, t_j.
errors: No mathematical error visible; the page is a definitional sketch.
The final map (repères → oriented faces) is left unfinished: the defining phrase is crossed out.
Notation is inconsistent. The repère is first written as a 4-tuple (D, S, ω, σ̄), then as a triple (D, s, ω) in the map. Also S_D = D ∩ S is written with capital S where an element s is meant.

ideas.what: Cell decomposition of the space of positions of an extra pseudoline relative to an arrangement: faces = stable (generic) positions, edges = semi-stable, vertices = critical.
ideas.modern_name: Extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid (one-element extensions / single-element liftings); cell structure of the space of pseudoline extensions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Las Vergnas (single-element extensions, 1978); Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993, extension spaces of rank-3 oriented matroids are homotopy 2-spheres); Mnëv–Ziegler

ideas.what: Flags/repères (critical position, vertex on it, orientations) with four operations σ1, σ, σ2, σ0, consecutive ones commuting, used to encode the 2-complex.
ideas.modern_name: Flag (dart) description of a combinatorial map / cartographic group; a cyclic Coxeter-type presentation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (cartographic group, Esquisse d'un programme 1984); Jones–Singerman (maps and groups, 1978)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un Programme (1984), §§ on cartographic groups and dessins d'enfants — for ordinary maps, not for pseudoline extension spaces

ideas.what: Map from repères to oriented faces: perturb a critical pseudoline off a vertex in a chosen direction to get an adjacent stable position.
ideas.modern_name: Triangle flip / mutation adjacent to a vertex of the extension space (local structure of the cell complex)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956) for triangle flips; oriented-matroid literature for mutations

missed.claim: Grothendieck treats the space of pseudoline positions relative to an arrangement (the rank-3 extension space) as a combinatorial map, with a flag set acted on by 'cartographic' operations. This links pseudoline / oriented-matroid extension spaces to the cartographic-group / dessins formalism he was developing at the same time in the Esquisse (1984). The later literature (Sturmfels–Ziegler 1993 and others) studies these spaces with order-complex and shellability methods, not cartographic-group actions.
missed.quote: arêtes biorientées i.e. repères : (D, S, ω, σ̄) où D p.v. critique ... Sommets : p.v. critiques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A flag/cartographic presentation of rank-3 extension spaces could give a group-theoretic handle on their topology (known to be S^2-like in rank 3), and possibly on the open questions in higher rank. It also concretely documents that the Esquisse cartographic formalism was applied by Grothendieck outside dessins.

missed.claim: The definition of the map from repères to oriented faces, and thereby the full flag structure of X̃, is begun but not completed on this page.
missed.quote: repères → faces orientées : (D, s, ω) ↦ la position voisine stable obtenue en ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only of minor interest; completing it is routine given the oriented-matroid mutation picture.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly a definitional dictionary, and its content anticipates known extension-space theory. The mildly notable point is Grothendieck's use of a map/flag (cartographic-group-like) formalism on pseudoline extension spaces, a viewpoint not taken in the later oriented-matroid literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 seems to read 'dont deux consécutifs commutant' (consistent with p.134: 'deux consécutifs commutant') rather than 'deux involutifs commutants'.
The space in line 1 is probably X̃^{ex} (as on p.134) rather than X̃^~.

'p.v.' is the abbreviation used throughout this page; p.134 uses 'p.r.'. Its expansion is unclear: it may relate to 'position voisine' (the phrase appears in full at the bottom) or to a pseudoline position.
The repère is (D, s, ω, σ̄) with s ∈ S_D = D ∩ S; 'σ̄ ori. de X en s' = an orientation of X at s.
The last line reads 'la position voisine stable obtenue en [crossed out]', with a stray 's' below 'repères'; it is not '$s$ obtenue'.
